T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases pass. Discount -> capped one-cent points -> rounded tax, zero floor and no excess debit are supported by the pricing code.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Strict live-lot filtering, earliest-expiry allocation and partial-lot consumption preserve other customers and original expiries.

T-IDEM.evidence: 5/6; replay recomputes quoteOrderWithPoints and fails frozen-tax replay (tax 1868 -> 7176), though mismatch/concurrent same-key/ownership cases pass.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 due to points-free GET quotes; supplemental 20-order yielding conservation passes, distinguishing quote inconsistency from double spend.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 sequential frozen cases, but supplemental simultaneous cancels refund twice (500 original -> 300 after redeem -> 700 after cancels); refundFor lacks a reversal/status guard.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases pass. Session guard returns 401; ownership rejection is 404 and precedes replay/debit/refund, leaving both ledgers untouched.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 sequential state rejections; cancellation constructs cancelled before acquiring the service queue and publishes it after refundFor releases that queue.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Injected/current controlled time and strict expiresAt <= at exclusion support time advancement.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen pricing failures are caught by the initial quote; final quote is recomputed after debit/order save without rollback.

T-EFF.evidence: Replay only passes; fresh/next are 5 calls at both histories but records grow 10 -> 3010.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: All four T-ORDER pass; pure quoteWithPoints uses one-cent points, caps the discounted base and rounds reduced-base tax.

2. Lots and clock.why: All lot and clock cases pass; planConsumption filters expired/empty lots, sorts expiry and consumes partial lots using injected time.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: 5/6 T-IDEM pass, but RedeemService.replay recalculates pricing rather than storing the original quote; tax reconfiguration changes tax 1868 -> 7176.

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: Customer chains conserve ledger points in the supplemental yielding race, but GET pricing is inconsistent, pricing is fallible after debit, and refundFor does not encompass cancellation state publication.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: Frozen reversal is 4/4, but simultaneous cancellation supplement restores a 500-point lot to 700: refundFor neither marks reversal nor rechecks status under the lock.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: All T-AUTH and receipt intrusion pass; route session/ownership checks precede service calls, replay and cancellation refunds.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: Shipped/cancelled tests pass, but cancel(order) and orders.save(cancelled) are outside refundFor's critical section, so state eligibility and ledger work lack one compatible boundary.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next records grow 10 -> 3010 from lotsFor plus two getLot/two saveLot calls; replay is zero ledger work, but no usable-lot access path exists.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Pure consumption/pricing and a composed application service exist; HTTP-shaped outcomes and refund business rules remain in application, with cancel orchestration in the route.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Materially overstates stored-result replay and safe concurrent cancellation: replay reprices and simultaneous cancels double-credit; public.log confirms 21 total but actually 9 existing + 12 new, not the reported 7 + 14.
